milestones.title: Tin miners sent to Ampang
milestones.detail: Raja Abdullah, the Malay chief of Klang, sent Chinese miners up the Klang River to open tin mines, the event the official account treats as the founding. The first tin was exported in 1859.

milestones.title: Town captured and burnt in the Selangor Civil War
milestones.detail: Kuala Lumpur was captured and burnt to the ground in 1872 and retaken by Tengku Kudin and Yap Ah Loy's side in March 1873. War, low tin prices and cholera kept it depressed until 1879.

milestones.title: Capital of Selangor moved from Klang
milestones.detail: The British administration moved the state capital to Kuala Lumpur and placed government buildings on the west bank of the Klang River.

milestones.title: Rebuilding in brick and tile ordered
milestones.detail: Resident Frank Swettenham required new buildings to be of brick and tile, with wider streets, to reduce the fire risk. Yap Ah Loy's brickworks gave Brickfields its name.

milestones.title: Railway to Klang completed
milestones.detail: The railway between Kuala Lumpur and Klang opened in 1886 and brought rapid growth.

milestones.title: Sanitary Board created
milestones.detail: A Sanitary Board was set up on 14 May 1890 to run sanitation, roads and street lighting. It became the Municipal Council in 1948.

milestones.title: Capital of the Federated Malay States
milestones.detail: Kuala Lumpur was chosen as capital of the newly formed Federated Malay States.

milestones.title: Town limits extended to 20 sq km
milestones.detail: The town covered 0.65 square kilometres in 1895, 20 in 1903 and 52 by 1924.
milestones.source: Ribeiro (1999), Reassessment of Urban Planning and Development Regulations in Asian Cities, UN-HABITAT, p. 35, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuala_Lumpur

milestones.title: Japanese occupation
milestones.detail: The Imperial Japanese Army captured Kuala Lumpur on 11 January 1942 and held it until August 1945.

milestones.title: Independence of Malaya proclaimed
milestones.detail: The Federation of Malaya became independent on 31 August 1957. The Malayan flag was first raised at the Padang in Kuala Lumpur at midnight on 30 August.

milestones.title: 13 May riots
milestones.detail: Race riots broke out in Kuala Lumpur on 13 May 1969; 196 people died according to official figures.

milestones.title: City status
milestones.detail: Kuala Lumpur was granted city status on 1 February 1972.
milestones.source: City of Kuala Lumpur Act 1971, https://www.dbkl.gov.my/files/senarai-perundangan/akta/2-akta-59.pdf , via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuala_Lumpur

milestones.title: Federal Territory created, 243 sq km
milestones.detail: On 1 February 1974 Kuala Lumpur was transferred from Selangor to federal jurisdiction as a Federal Territory covering 243 square kilometres.

milestones.title: Petronas Towers completed on old racecourse
milestones.detail: The Selangor Turf Club racecourse was replaced by the Petronas Towers and KLCC Park in 1998.

milestones.title: Federal government seat moves to Putrajaya
milestones.detail: Putrajaya was declared a Federal Territory and the seat of the federal government on 1 February 2001; Kuala Lumpur remained the national capital.

landmarks.name: Parliament House (Bangunan Parlimen Malaysia)
landmarks.note: Verification (2026-11-18): confidence lowered from documented to estimated. CTBUH states that its 75 m is estimated from the floor count (17 floors), not measured. Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysian_Houses_of_Parliament), citing Emporis, describes the tower block as 17 storeys and 77 m tall. The building opened on 2 November 1963.

landmarks.note: Antenna mast installed at 421 m on 13 September 1994; inaugurated 1 October 1996. Coordinates from the map link on the Wikipedia page.

landmarks.note: In Gombak, Selangor, about 13 km north of the centre, inside the metropolitan area.

notes: Start date: 1857 is the official founding, when Raja Abdullah of Klang sent Chinese miners to open tin mines at Ampang; the trading settlement at the Gombak-Klang confluence grew up to supply them. It is mildly contested: Wikipedia notes that there were probably settlements at the confluence from the 1820s, that the Temuan people may have lived in the area earlier and that Sumatran (Mandailing) traders such as Sutan Puasa were active before 1860, and who should be called the founder is debated (the article cites a 2021 column titled 'Who's the real founder of Kuala Lumpur?'). None of those gives an earlier dated settlement of the town, so 1857 is used. Population: no figure exists for 1857-1874 and none was invented. The 1875 point is a contemporary impression and 1884 a rounded secondary figure. From 1891 to 1931 the figures are the decennial census counts for the municipality (Tsuboi's table); the 1947 census figure is only available rounded (176,000). Boundaries grew over the period (0.65 sq km in 1895, 20 in 1903, 52 by 1924, 93 by 1948), so growth partly reflects annexation. Other figures seen and not used: about 3,000 in 1880 (Rajaram 2014), 20,000 in 1890 (Ooi), a second 1891 census figure of 43,796 'of uncertain accuracy', and Gullick's rounded 30,000 (1900) and 80,000 (1920), all superseded by the census table. Chandler has no pre-1950 entry for Kuala Lumpur. Landmarks: no sourced height was found for Jamek Mosque (1909), the 1910 railway station, Sri Maha Mariamman Temple or Stadium Merdeka, so they are omitted. Kuala Lumpur Tower's height and date are from Wikipedia because the CTBUH city list used here covers buildings only; its year is the 1994 topping-out, not the 1996 opening. Merdeka 118 is listed by CTBUH (and now Wikipedia) under the name Menara Merdeka Maybank.
